q: What is the «fifth taste», alongside sweet, sour, salty and bitter, called?
explanation: Umami is the savoury taste of glutamate.

q: Which cheese is traditionally used in a Greek salad?
explanation: A Greek salad contains feta.

q: Who discovered penicillin?
explanation: Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928.

q: Which vitamin is needed for blood clotting?
explanation: Vitamin K takes part in blood clotting.

q: Who invented the World Wide Web?
explanation: Berners-Lee proposed the Web in 1989.

q: What does the term «open source» mean?
options: The code can be read and modified
explanation: Anyone can study and modify open-source code.

q: In which unit is the loudness of sound usually measured?
explanation: Loudness is measured in decibels.

q: How many letters are there in the English alphabet?
explanation: The English alphabet has 26 letters.

q: Which country was the first to give women the vote in national elections (1893)?
explanation: New Zealand did so in 1893.

q: Which star, apart from the Sun, is closest to Earth?
explanation: Proxima Centauri is about 4.2 light-years away.

q: What does the science of entomology study?
explanation: Entomology is the branch of zoology that studies insects.

q: What is the approximate speed of light in a vacuum?
explanation: The speed of light in a vacuum is about 299,792 km/s.

q: What is the change in direction of a light ray passing from air into water called?
explanation: Refraction occurs at the boundary between media of different optical density.

q: Which country has the longest coastline in the world?
explanation: Canada's coastline is over 200,000 km including its islands.

q: Which lake is shared by Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania?
explanation: Lake Victoria is the largest lake in Africa.

q: Which two countries fought the Hundred Years' War (1337–1453)?
explanation: English and French kings fought over the French throne and lands.

q: Which people carved the ancient city of Petra, in present-day Jordan, into the rock?
explanation: Petra was the capital of the Nabataean Kingdom.

q: What is the 1215 document that limited the power of the English king called?
explanation: King John signed the Magna Carta.

q: Who wrote the novel «Fathers and Sons»?
explanation: Turgenev's novel was published in 1862.

q: Who created the detective Sherlock Holmes?
explanation: The first Holmes story appeared in 1887.

q: Which painter created «The Starry Night»?
explanation: Van Gogh painted it in 1889.

q: In which Paris museum is the «Mona Lisa» kept?
explanation: Leonardo da Vinci's «Mona Lisa» is in the Louvre.

q: Who composed the opera «La traviata»?
explanation: Verdi's «La traviata» premiered in 1853.

q: How many lines does a musical staff have?
explanation: A musical staff has five lines.

q: Who played the title role in «Forrest Gump» (1994)?
explanation: Tom Hanks played Forrest Gump and won an Oscar for it.

q: Which 1997 film by James Cameron won 11 Oscars?
explanation: «Titanic» shares the record for Oscar wins: 11.

q: In which country was the first football World Cup held in 1930?
explanation: Uruguay hosted and won the first World Cup.

q: Who became world chess champion in 1985 by beating Anatoly Karpov?
explanation: Kasparov became world champion in 1985 at the age of 22.

q: Which spice is considered the most expensive in the world by weight?
explanation: Saffron is harvested by hand from crocus stigmas.

q: Which grain is traditionally used to make Japanese sake?
explanation: Sake is made by fermenting rice.

q: Which blood group (ABO system) is the «universal donor» for red blood cells?
explanation: Group O red blood cells suit most recipients.

q: How many bones does an adult human skeleton have?
explanation: An adult human has 206 bones.

q: What does the abbreviation PDF stand for?
explanation: PDF is a portable document format created by Adobe.

q: What is malware that encrypts your files and demands a payment called?
explanation: This kind of malware is called ransomware.

q: How many hours are there in one week?
explanation: 24 hours × 7 days = 168 hours.

q: How many minutes are there in a day?
explanation: 24 hours × 60 minutes = 1,440 minutes.

q: What are homonyms?
options: Same spelling and sound, but different meanings
explanation: For example, a «bank» of a river and a «bank» for money.

q: How many cases does Russian have (in standard school grammar)?
explanation: School grammar lists six cases, from nominative to prepositional.

q: Which UN body has five permanent members with veto power?
explanation: The permanent members are China, France, Russia, the UK and the US.

q: Which of these countries is not a member of the European Union?
explanation: Norway is not in the EU, though it belongs to the European Economic Area.

q: Which elementary particle carries the electromagnetic force?
explanation: The photon is the quantum of the electromagnetic field.

q: Which of Newton's laws says that every action has an equal and opposite reaction?
explanation: This is Newton's third law of motion.

q: Which planet in the Solar System rotates «on its side», with an axial tilt of about 98°?
explanation: Uranus's axis lies almost in the plane of its orbit.

q: Which city is the capital of Kazakhstan?
explanation: The capital is Astana; Almaty is the largest city.

q: Which desert runs along the Atlantic coast of Namibia?
explanation: The Namib is one of the oldest deserts in the world.

q: Which of these countries does the equator pass through?
explanation: The equator crosses Ecuador (the name itself means «equator»); Peru, Venezuela and Tanzania are off the line.

q: Which 1648 peace ended the Thirty Years' War?
explanation: The Peace of Westphalia laid the foundations of the European state system.

q: Who became the first emperor of unified China in 221 BC?
explanation: Qin Shi Huang united the warring states into a single empire.

q: Whose empire did Hernán Cortés conquer in 1519–1521?
explanation: Cortés took the Aztec capital Tenochtitlan in 1521.

q: Who wrote the novel «The Master and Margarita»?
explanation: Bulgakov worked on the novel from the late 1920s until his death in 1940.

q: Who wrote the novel «Wuthering Heights»?
explanation: Emily Brontë's novel was published in 1847.

q: Who painted «Black Square»?
explanation: Malevich first showed «Black Square» in 1915.

q: In which Italian city is the Uffizi Gallery located?
explanation: The Uffizi in Florence holds Renaissance masterpieces.

q: Who composed the opera cycle «The Ring of the Nibelung»?
explanation: Wagner worked on the tetralogy for about 26 years.

q: Which of these tempo markings is the fastest?
explanation: Presto means very fast.

q: Which film is considered the first feature-length talkie (1927)?
explanation: «The Jazz Singer» opened the era of sound film.

q: Which country gave the world the cinematic «New Wave» (Godard, Truffaut)?
explanation: The New Wave emerged in France in the late 1950s.

q: How many players per team are on the field at once in rugby union?
explanation: Rugby union fields 15 players per team.

q: What surface is used at the French Open (Roland Garros)?
explanation: Roland Garros is played on red clay.

q: Which plant produces vanilla pods?
explanation: Vanilla comes from the pods of an orchid of the genus Vanilla.

q: What is the Italian dessert made of mascarpone, coffee and ladyfingers called?
explanation: Tiramisu means «pick me up» in Italian.

q: Which hormone is produced in darkness and regulates the sleep cycle?
explanation: Melatonin is produced by the pineal gland.

q: A deficiency of which vitamin causes scurvy?
explanation: Scurvy results from a long-term lack of vitamin C.

q: What does the abbreviation SSD stand for?
explanation: An SSD stores data in flash memory chips.

q: Which prefix in a web address shows a secure connection?
explanation: HTTPS encrypts data between the browser and the site.

q: In which month does the summer solstice fall in the Northern Hemisphere?
explanation: The longest day of the year is around 21 June.

q: What temperature in Celsius corresponds to 32 °F?
explanation: 32 °F is the freezing point of water, 0 °C.

q: Which language family does Russian belong to?
explanation: Russian belongs to the Slavic branch of the Indo-European family.

q: What is the Japanese syllabary mainly used to write foreign loanwords called?
explanation: Katakana is used for loanwords and foreign names.

q: What is inflation?
options: A fall in the general price level
A rise in the general price level
explanation: With inflation, the same amount of money buys fewer goods.

q: In which city is the NATO headquarters located?
explanation: NATO's headquarters is in Brussels.

q: Which chemical element has atomic number 6 and underlies organic chemistry?
explanation: Carbon is the basis of organic compounds.

q: What does Avogadro's number (about 6.02·10²³) represent?
options: The number of atoms in the Sun
The number of particles in one mole of a substance
The speed of light in a vacuum
explanation: One mole of a substance contains about 6.02·10²³ elementary particles.

q: What does the redshift in the spectra of distant galaxies usually indicate?
options: That they are moving toward us
That they are moving away from us
explanation: Redshift is linked to the expansion of the Universe.

q: In which country is the legendary city of Timbuktu?
explanation: Timbuktu is an ancient trading and learning centre on the southern edge of the Sahara.

q: Which is the largest island in the world, not counting continents?
explanation: Greenland covers more than 2 million km².

q: Which canal links the Mediterranean and the Red Sea?
explanation: The Suez Canal opened in 1869.

q: Who won the Battle of Hastings in 1066?
explanation: William of Normandy won and became King of England.

q: In which year did the Ottomans capture Constantinople?
explanation: Mehmed II took the city on 29 May 1453, ending the Byzantine Empire.

q: Which 1494 treaty divided the spheres of influence of Spain and Portugal?
explanation: The treaty drew a line along a meridian in the Atlantic.

q: Who wrote the novel «Dracula» (1897)?
explanation: Bram Stoker's novel was published in 1897.

q: Who wrote the novel «Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus»?
explanation: Mary Shelley published the novel in 1818.

q: Who painted «The Scream» (1893)?
explanation: Munch made several versions of «The Scream».

q: Which architectural style features pointed arches and stained glass, as in Notre-Dame?
explanation: Gothic architecture is known for pointed vaults and large stained-glass windows.

q: Who composed the «St Matthew Passion»?
explanation: Bach wrote the «St Matthew Passion» in the 1720s.

q: What is a piece for a solo instrument accompanied by an orchestra called?
explanation: In a concerto the soloist interacts with the orchestra.

q: Who directed «Blade Runner» (1982)?
explanation: Ridley Scott directed it, based on a novel by Philip K. Dick.

q: Which actor played Vito Corleone in «The Godfather» (1972)?
explanation: Brando won an Oscar for the role.

q: How many points does a touchdown score in American football?
explanation: A touchdown is worth 6 points, with an extra-point attempt to follow.

q: Who was the first person to run a mile in under four minutes, in 1954?
explanation: Bannister ran 3:59.4 in Oxford on 6 May 1954.

q: Which grain is the main ingredient of bourbon whiskey?
explanation: US rules require a bourbon grain mix to be at least 51% corn.

q: What is the French sauce of egg yolks and butter served with eggs Benedict called?
explanation: Hollandaise is the classic sauce for eggs Benedict.

q: Which human organ produces bile?
explanation: Bile is produced by the liver and stored in the gallbladder.

q: Which vitamin is produced in the skin under sunlight?
explanation: Ultraviolet light triggers vitamin D synthesis in the skin.

q: Who is considered the first programmer for writing an algorithm for Babbage's Analytical Engine?
explanation: Ada Lovelace described an algorithm for Bernoulli numbers in 1843.

q: What does RAM stand for?
explanation: RAM is fast, volatile memory used by running programs.

q: How many seconds are there in a day?
How many hours are there in a leap year?
explanation: 366 days × 24 hours = 8,784 hours.

q: What is the official language of Brazil?
explanation: Brazil is the largest Portuguese-speaking country in the world.

q: What is a palindrome?
options: A word with the opposite meaning
A word or phrase that reads the same in both directions
A word formed by shortening a phrase
explanation: For example, «level» or «A man, a plan, a canal: Panama».

q: Which UN document adopted in 1948 proclaimed basic human rights?
options: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights
explanation: The UN General Assembly adopted it on 10 December 1948.

q: Which institution sets monetary policy for the eurozone?
explanation: The European Central Bank is based in Frankfurt.
